chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The lodging upon the people of the taxation is for three days.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْخَرَاجِ: People of the taxation (those subject to land tax)

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum duration for tax collectors to stay among the people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) sets a specific legal limit of three days for the lodging of tax collectors (ahl al-kharaj) among the populace, a ruling designed to prevent the abuse of power and excessive financial burden on subjects. This duration reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on justice in governance, ensuring that state officials do not overstay their mandate or impose undue hardship on the community they serve.
